alt: Nicolas Hernandez emailed TracFone's fccassist on May 31, 2026, at 7:16 PM, rejecting their final position dated May 31, 2026, regarding a Motorola Moto G Play 2024 (IMEI 3198) permanently Network Unlocked under Ticket ID 1338984705, and threatening to escalate the matter to the FCC under Case File 8711384 for an unresolved firmware restriction.
summary: This document is a formal email response from Nicolas Hernandez to the TracFone/Straight Talk Executive Resolution Department, dated May 31, 2026. The correspondence formally rejects the carrier's final position regarding firmware and bootloader restrictions on a fully-owned Motorola Moto G Play 2024. Forensically, this record establishes the member's technical rebuttal to anti-consumer lock-in strategies, citing specific misapplications of service terms and contradictory hardware-software profiles. It serves as the final procedural step before further federal escalation in the telecommunications segment of the audit.

- <EEEEEEE © gmail.com> Sun, May 31, 2026 at 7:16 PM
To: "fecassist@tracfone.com" <fccassist@tracfone.com>

To Samuel and the Executive Resolution Department,

Thank you for confirming the correct hardware details and verifying that this Motorola Moto G
Play 2024 (IMEI ending in 3198) is permanently Network Unlocked under Ticket ID:
1338984705.

| am writing to formally reject the carrier’s final position dated May 31, 2026. Your technical and
policy justifications for maintaining a secondary firmware restriction on this fully owned hardware
are invalid for the following reasons:

1. Misapplication of Terms of Service Constraints: You cite Section Ill, Clause 13 of the Terms
and Conditions of Service to restrict bootloader modifications. However, because this device has
fully satisfied its network tenure and is entirely paid off, utilizing an OEM-sanctioned utility
(Motorola's official bootloader unlock program) to modify user-owned hardware does not
interfere with active service delivery or network integrity. Relying on service terms to indefinitely
restrict core hardware access on fully owned devices constitutes an anti-consumer lock-in
strategy.

2. Contradictory Software Profile Responsibility: You assert that this secure-boot partition
restriction is compiled entirely at the factory level by the Original Equipment Manufacturer
(OEM) and that Straight Talk lacks the engineering mechanisms to override it. However, the
OEM explicitly provides valid cryptographic unlock keys for this model, noting that the execution
loop is triggered specifically by carrier-customized software profiles requested by TracFone. The
carrier cannot divest itself of responsibility for restrictions built into its own custom software
distributions.

3. Notice of Intent to Escalate: If the carrier refuses to coordinate a technical resolution with the
OEM to clear this carrier-enforced loop, | will decline administrative closure of this file and
formally escalate this matter by filing a Formal FCC Complaint and initiating a Mandatory
Arbitration Notice of Dispute under Section II of the carrier's agreement, forcing a formal legal
accounting of these proprietary firmware restrictions.

Desired Outcome:
| require TracFone to coordinate with the OEM to clear the carrier-side firmware profile blocking

the secure boot partition, or provide an unrestricted hardware variant. Please ensure this entire
correspondence is appended to FCC Case File 8711384.

Sincerely,

Nicolas Hernandez
